To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have performed a comprehensive analysis of CNV data from ASD subjects from AutDB, an ASD genetic database that contains CNV data from 48 scientific papers, and identified 11 genomic loci with an excess of CNVs in ASD subjects.

(1) CNVs in ASD subjects are significantly larger than those in control individuals, (2) CNVs in the ASD population are enriched at 11 genomic loci, (3) 15q11-13 is comprised of three distinct CNV loci associated with ASD, (4) the CNVs at these loci show different inheritance patterns, and (5) CNVs in 15q11q13 overlap with CNVs in control individuals to different degrees.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of copy number variants (CNV) in autism spectrum disorder (autism) and their association with the disorder.
the analysis and characterization of CNV data from a large number of scientific reports on ASD individuals.

the analysis of multi-studied genome-wide CNV (copy number variation) data from AutDB, a genetic database that contains detailed annotations of published reports of CNV loci identified in ASD subjects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data presented in this manuscript is valuable for clinical and research purposes.
there are 11 copy number variant (CNV) loci with an excess in ASD subjects, with a total of 166 genes.
there is an increased burden of CNVs in the ASD population compared to control populations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified 11 CNV loci in the AutDB dataset that are associated with ASD.
the AutDB database, with a large collection of CNV data, provides an important resource for the genetic study of ASD.
we identified a set of CNV loci in the ASD population, that are significantly different from those in the control population.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AutDB can be used to prioritize candidate CNV loci for ASD, and that the CNV loci associated with ASD are heterogeneous in size, genomic location and gene content.
the AutDB CNV database provides an invaluable resource for the genetic analysis of autism.
AutDB provides a valuable resource to study CNVs in autism, and the results presented here are a good starting point for future genetic analyses of ASD.
